title: He raised a prophet…
paragraphs:
He raised a prophet…
but could not raise his own sons.

Because this is not just Eli’s story.
This is a mirror.
And something in you already knows it.

You can stand close to holy things…
and still be far from God.

You can mentor someone into destiny…
while quietly neglecting your own obedience.

You can teach truth…
and tolerate sin at the same time.

An old priest.
Eyes dimming.
Hands familiar with sacred rituals.
A lifetime in the temple.

Men who wore priestly garments…
but had no reverence for the God they claimed to serve.

“Now the sons of Eli were worthless men. They did not know the Lord.”
—1 Samuel 2:12

They worked in God’s house…
but did not know God.

He heard the reports.
He saw the corruption.
He spoke words of rebuke—
but he did not act with the weight of obedience.

“Why then do you scorn my sacrifices…? …You honor your sons above me.”
—1 Samuel 2:29

Not because Eli hated God—
but because he tolerated what God hated.
Now here comes the tension that should shake every leader, every parent, every believer:
While Eli was failing in his own house…
In the quiet of the night, God called.
Until finally, the old priest realized—
And Eli said the words that would echo through history:

“Speak, Lord, for your servant hears.”
—1 Samuel 3:9

Eli—
a man under judgment—
still helped a boy hear God’s voice.

God can still use your voice…
even while confronting your compromise.

You can preach and still be drifting.
You can serve and still be hiding.
You can guide others…
while ignoring what God is telling you.
Because Eli’s issue was not ignorance.
A quiet refusal to fully obey.

And passivity in the face of sin…
is still rebellion.
But don’t look at Eli and feel only condemnation.
Because the story is not finished.
Eli was a priest who failed.
But Jesus is the Priest who never will.

“Because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.”
—Hebrews 7:24
Eli could not cleanse his house.

“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree.”
—1 Peter 2:24
Eli sat trembling when judgment came.

Jesus stood in your place
and absorbed that judgment on the cross.
Where Eli failed to restrain sin—
And this is where the shift happens.
But conviction that calls you back.
Maybe you feel exposed reading this.

You know the areas you’ve “managed”…
instead of surrendered.
God is not exposing you to destroy you.
He is exposing you to redeem you.
Samuel heard God’s voice in the night.
you don’t have to fear the night anymore.
Because grace speaks louder than failure.
Don’t soften what God is confronting.
Don’t stay comfortable in what Jesus died to free you from.
Because the same God who called Samuel…
He’s not just calling you to listen.

Where have I been near God’s work…
but far from God’s will?
Where have I chosen comfort over obedience?
Where have I honored people… above God?
If this stirred something in you…
